'''Phase II clone trooper armor''' was an enhanced version of the [[Phase I clone trooper armor/Legends|Phase I]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] armor, used by the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. After the Clone Wars, it was retained by the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of the newly-formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], but was gradually replaced by new [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|stormtrooper armor]].

==Description==
[[File:PhaseIIArmor-SM.png|thumb|left|220px|[[Halle Burtoni/Legends|Halle Burtoni]] showing a Phase II armor hologram.]]
Phase II incorporated all of its predecessor's systems in addition to polarized lenses, padding, and stronger, lighter armor plates. It could also support more modular attachments, making it superior to its predecessor. Unlike early iterations of the Phase I armor, color was used to denote unit affiliation instead of rank.

Phase II armor was introduced around [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Republic 68" /> and by [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]] it had slowly replaced Phase I armor. Phase II armor was the basis of the [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|stormtrooper armor]] later worn by the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|soldiers]] of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. Another variant of the Phase II armor was the [[Katarn armor]]. [[ARC trooper armor/Legends|ARC trooper armor]] was also modified to be Phase II.

The new armor incorporated a more advanced air filtration and oxygen supply system, polarized lenses, and an [[annunciator]] to make speech more comprehensible. In addition, the boots were magnetized and incorporated a [[grav-field alternator]] to ensure stability. Another useful feature was that the [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and the bodysuit could be pressurized, providing temporary protection against non-breathable atmospheres. It was not as pressurized as its predecessor, however, when used in conjunction with a [[Breathmask survival gear|external respirator]], the clones could last longer in a vacuum environment wearing Phase 2 compared to its predecessor.

==Variations==
[[File:Clone_Troopers_Phase_II.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Different variations of Phase II armor.]]
The Phase II armor, unlike the Phase I armor, had many distinct variations. In some examples, armor was modified to suit an individual clone, while in others, it was specialized to suit a specific 'breed' of troopers (such as [[Clone paratrooper/Legends|clone paratroopers]]). It is known that some clones, like [[Faie/Legends|Faie]] and [[Gree (clone trooper)/Legends|Gree]], had more than one set of armor. Many [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone trooper commanders]], [[Clone commando/Legends|Clone commandos]] and [[Clone shadow trooper/Legends|Shadow Clone Troopers]] had special attachments on their armor, and allowed some lower ranked officers to wear special attachments as well. Some special attachments included [[Kama/Legends|kamas]] and [[Pauldron/Legends|pauldrons]], they could also attach electrobinoculars and sun visors to their helmets. Clone captains would occasionally have a pair of [[DC-17 hand blaster/Legends|DC-17 hand blasters]] attached to each side of their kama.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Concept.png|thumb|300px|left|Concept art]]
The Phase II [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone trooper pilots]]' helmets were meant to be a fusion between the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] pilots' helmets and the [[TIE pilot]]s' helmets, both seen in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Episode III: Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>. The helmet of the main Phase II Clone Trooper is a fusion of the Stormtrooper helmet and [[Phase I clone trooper armor/Legends|Phase I clone trooper armor]] helmet.

That Boba Fett's armor originally had some connection to the stormtrooper pedigree had long been a vague assertion in Star Wars lore. Design Director Doug Chiang's concept art focused on this connection, melding features of both armors into the finished clone trooper design. R. Kim Smith and Michael Patrick Murnane built a concept model of the clone trooper which implied that the first generation armor was thicker and bulkier than the lighter armor worn by the stormtroopers. This design concept was carried through by the Episode III Art Department, that further progressed the look of the clone troopers closer to the stormtroopers of the original trilogy, including variant designs that gave obvious nods to the sandtrooper, scout trooper and snowtrooper designs.<ref name="DB-clone troopers">{{DB|organization|clonetroopers|clone troopers}}</ref>
